title: Synthetic Time-to-Event Manuscript Review Packet

studies.studyTitle: Registry claim: immunotherapy extends overall survival

findings.studyTitle: Registry claim: immunotherapy extends overall survival
findings.evidence: Exposure begins after baseline with a median start lag of 43 days, but the model treats exposure as baseline-fixed.
findings.action: Recast exposure as time-dependent or add a justified landmark analysis with sensitivity checks.

findings.studyTitle: Registry claim: immunotherapy extends overall survival
findings.evidence: Schoenfeld p=0.018 indicates a proportional-hazards violation, but no time-varying effect model is reported.
findings.action: Add proportional-hazards diagnostics and use stratified or time-varying coefficients when assumptions fail.

findings.studyTitle: Registry claim: immunotherapy extends overall survival
findings.evidence: Censoring differs by 18% across arms (immunotherapy: 32%, standard care: 14%).
findings.action: Report censoring reasons by arm and add inverse-probability or sensitivity analyses.

findings.studyTitle: Registry claim: immunotherapy extends overall survival
findings.evidence: At least one arm has 32% censoring, but no censoring table is included.
findings.action: Add a table separating administrative censoring, withdrawal, loss to follow-up, and competing events.

findings.studyTitle: Registry claim: immunotherapy extends overall survival
findings.evidence: 66 events across 16 modeled covariates gives 4.1 events per variable.
findings.action: Reduce model complexity, pre-specify covariates, or provide penalized-regression sensitivity analysis.

findings.studyTitle: Registry claim: immunotherapy extends overall survival
findings.evidence: A competing terminal event is present, but the analysis does not use cumulative incidence or cause-specific/subdistribution hazard methods.
findings.action: Add competing-risk analysis and show whether the treatment conclusion changes.

findings.studyTitle: Registry claim: immunotherapy extends overall survival
findings.evidence: The shortest follow-up-to-event-time ratio is 0.69, so median follow-up may not support the stated survival horizon.
findings.action: Extend follow-up or soften claims that depend on longer event windows.

findings.studyTitle: Registry claim: immunotherapy extends overall survival
findings.evidence: The manuscript makes directional survival-benefit claims while high-severity survival review holds remain unresolved.
findings.action: Change the claim to hypothesis-generating language until endpoint and model assumptions are cleared.

reproducibilityActions: Add cumulative-incidence or competing-risk model output alongside Kaplan-Meier estimates.
Commit a model-specification manifest with event counts, covariate list, and penalization settings.
Export proportional-hazards diagnostics and time-varying coefficient sensitivity plots.
Publish arm-level censoring reasons and repeat estimates with censoring sensitivity weights.
Re-run the model with exposure encoded as time-dependent and compare hazard ratios.
researchGapPrompts: Compare disease areas where informative censoring changes survival conclusions after inverse-probability weighting.
Find clinical trial families with recurring proportional-hazards violations and summarize accepted alternative estimands.
Identify endpoints where competing-risk models reverse ordinary Kaplan-Meier interpretations.
Map studies that treat post-baseline treatment initiation as baseline exposure and estimate the direction of immortal-time bias.
